_about: One entry per numbered rule of book/03-page-rulebook.md and per row of the owner rules (book/02-owner-rules.md; a project may add rows in its own OWNER-RULES.md). enforcement 'code': the checks decide it. 'judgment': a person decides; the proxy checks are code that prove the evidence exists. Severity FAIL unless warn_reason says why. 'needs' says what the checks read: live (the served page), project (the project folder), nextjs (the site's code; adapters/nextjs, run only when growth.json stack is nextjs). 'files' is kept in step by growth registry_sync. tests/ fail when a rule has no entry or an entry names a check that does not exist.

rules.rule: No shortcuts: every step of the job's playbook, in order, with every owner check-in.
Pre-flight before the build: planning complete, shared site problems fixed first, every checkpoint set
Proof by data. State no number, customer, price, award, case study or guarantee that the business has not already stated or the owner has not approved.
rules.why_judgment: Whether a number or claim was ever stated or approved needs a person to trace it; the proxy blocks prices, banned customers and a missing fact check.

rules.rule: Name no customer, show no logo and quote nobody unless the owner confirms it is real and allowed.
rules.why_judgment: Whether a quote or logo is real and allowed needs the owner; the proxy blocks the known hidden customers and implied lists.

rules.rule: What the business says about itself reads the same on every page.
rules.why_judgment: Matching every self-claim to BRAND.md wording needs reading; the proxy blocks BRAND 7's never-claims and prices.

rules.rule: One length for the call (or the one booking step), everywhere
Every fact about another product, a law or a rule comes from its official source, checked today, and the page says where it came from.
rules.why_judgment: Checking a fact against its official source needs a reader; the proxy requires a dated fact-check file.

rules.rule: A page must be true today before you promote, redesign or link to it.
rules.why_judgment: Truth today needs a reader; the proxy requires a fact check within 30 days.

rules.rule: Quote a vendor's price for the reader's size and billing, not for the size the vendor's page opens with.
rules.why_judgment: A vendor's price for the reader's size needs a reader on the vendor page; the proxy requires the fact-check file.

rules.rule: Say plainly what is free, limited, metered or paid, where it is true, near the top and not under a price table.
rules.why_judgment: What is free, limited or metered is a fact about a product; the proxy requires the fact-check file.

rules.rule: If a page contradicts itself, or a fact about the business is missing from the list, ask the owner.
rules.why_judgment: Spotting a contradiction needs a reader; the proxy fails while a question for the page sits open over 7 days.

rules.rule: Key takeaways, side boxes, stat highlights and calculators restate what the page already says.
rules.why_judgment: A box restating the text is meaning; the proxy fails any number that appears only in a box.

rules.rule: Ship no placeholder text and no leftovers.
Every page says when it was written and last changed, and the dates are true.
A title must not tell a story the page cannot source.
rules.why_judgment: Whether a title's story is sourced needs a reader; the proxy requires the fact-check file.

rules.rule: Do not promise user reviews, quotes or ratings the page cannot quote.
About and Contact answer what a buyer asks before booking.
rules.why_judgment: Which buyer questions About/Contact must answer is the owner's knowledge; the proxy requires the research file.

rules.rule: When you review or compare, say who you are first
Every claim you audit gets an outcome, written in the pull request: fixed, removed, reworded, or kept with a reason and a source.
rules.why_judgment: A claim's outcome is a judgment; the proxy requires the page's journal (the record before the pull request).

rules.rule: Write down the reader's question before you write the page, and answer it in the first screen.
One page answers one question.
rules.why_judgment: Whether two pages answer one question needs search-intent reading; the proxy requires the dossier (section A5 lists our own competing pages).

rules.rule: When the title is a question, the first line is the answer
Answer with the reader's own number where one exists
rules.why_judgment: Using the reader's own number is a writing choice; the proxy requires the page's tool with its state in the URL.

rules.rule: Sell only to the reader who needs it.
rules.why_judgment: Which reader is buying is intent; the proxy requires the dossier and a reason line on each call.

rules.rule: The offer's heading, button, body and form agree.
rules.why_judgment: Heading/button/body agreement is meaning; the proxy enforces one label with its reason line.

rules.rule: When one page serves different readers, let the reader pick their case and give each a route.
rules.why_judgment: Routing readers by case is design; the proxy requires a URL-state picker.

rules.rule: A table of limits, routes or prices has a source on every row, a check date, and what it means for the reader.
A hub is a map of where the reader is, not a second copy of its posts.
A new cluster or service starts with research, not a template
rules.why_judgment: Research quality needs a reader; the proxy requires the 32-question dossier and an independent review.

rules.rule: Depth, not length.
rules.why_judgment: Depth vs length is judgment; the proxy fails repeated folds.

rules.rule: An About page is a story that earns trust, not a list of buzzwords.
rules.why_judgment: Trust in a story is judgment; the proxy blocks hype words.

rules.rule: No two folds of a page look alike.
rules.why_judgment: Looking alike is visual; the proxy fails folds with the same structure and requires fresh screenshots.

rules.rule: A money page states only what the site already states.
rules.why_judgment: Every number's source needs tracing; the proxy blocks prices, banned customers and never-claims.

rules.rule: Every call to action goes through the one conversion path the site uses (a booking, a quote form or the contact form)
Every booking button gives a reason to act
One primary button style per page
The primary CTA carries a soft glow in its own colour
Link and button text names its one target.
No internal link carries `utm_` parameters
Every money page has a scroll-in sticky call bar
Every money page has a relevant exit offer
Every internal text link on the site previews its target with a small "+"
Every page passes the technical SEO check before release
Every list tick is a tick inside a circle
Every fold has its own surface, chosen by its job in the reader's mind
Every picture and chart reads in 3 seconds
rules.why_judgment: Whether a picture is clear is a human read; the proxy requires 1366 and 390 shots newer than the last commit.

rules.rule: A fold-by-fold detail plan comes before any page work
Every page is archived live before and after it changes
A rework removes what it replaced
Every page has one named author, linked
Never state where the business or its people are, when `BRAND.md` says not to
Every control reads in every state: at rest, on hover and on keyboard focus
Ready for AI answers (GEO/AEO)
Show the reader where to interact
A trust line states only what the site states elsewhere.
A form that creates a lead must prove a person sent it
The contact page puts the form first and does not leave half the screen empty.
At desktop width there is no empty half, no tiny logos and no stretched illustration.
rules.why_judgment: Empty halves and tiny logos are visual; the proxy requires fresh 1280 and 1920 screenshots.

rules.rule: Stay in your lane in the site repo.
rules.why_judgment: Lane ownership is coordination; the proxy requires work on its own branch.

rules.rule: Use the site's design system: its tokens, its shared layout styles and its content look
Keep the approved logo lockup as it is.
One header, one footer and one reading column on every page of a kind.
rules.why_judgment: That nothing moves between pages needs a browser; the proxy requires one shared frame and fresh shots at every width.

rules.rule: Everything in an article ends on one right edge, at one reading width
rules.why_judgment: One right edge is visual; the proxy requires fresh shots at every width.

rules.rule: Body text is 60 to 80 characters a line.
Cards in a row share the row.
rules.why_judgment: Row sharing is visual; the proxy requires fresh shots.

rules.rule: A popover, menu or sticky bar never covers something the reader needs to click.
rules.why_judgment: Covering a control is visual; the proxy requires shots and a click-through.

rules.rule: Wide tables scroll inside their own box, keep the first column sticky, show an edge shadow and cut nothing off.
Every page has a type, and the type sets its frame:
Breadcrumbs sit on every page except home, and come from the same data as the BreadcrumbList markup.
One footer, full width, on every page.
Build components and apply them by pattern; do not build one-off code for one page.
rules.why_judgment: Whether a block is reusable is design; the proxy requires the shared components and fails page-local copies.

rules.rule: The contents list is built from the article's H2s.
One "Read next" section under each post, with relevant stories and no duplicate sections.
Engagement blocks (pickers, quizzes, calculators, checklists) are built from the page's own content.
rules.why_judgment: An engagement block adding no claim is meaning; the proxy checks reduced motion and box numbers.

rules.rule: Embeds (maps, videos, widgets) load on a click or when needed, and send nothing to a third party before the reader acts.
One icon family, no emoji in the interface or in tables.
Motion is made with CSS and a little script, not with animation libraries.
Readable beats pretty.
rules.why_judgment: Contrast needs the rendered colours (rule 153 adds the CSS check once Playwright is allowed); the proxy requires fresh shots.

rules.rule: A link inside running text is underlined, not shown by colour alone.
rules.why_judgment: Underlines are computed styles; the proxy requires fresh shots.

rules.rule: Every article has its own original cover, and no picture has the page's title drawn into it.
rules.why_judgment: Originality is judgment; the proxy requires a cover with alt text (the site repo's cover test checks hashes).

rules.rule: Every image has alt text. A decorative image is marked decorative.
No picture served is heavier than 200 KiB, and each has width and height.
Every image file keeps its extension in its name.
A page's share image exists, is the real size it says, and is never a loader, a sprite or a GIF.
Nothing on the first screen loads lazily, and the main picture has priority.
Nothing scrolls by itself while a page loads.
A phone screen holds the page in every state, not only the settled one.
rules.why_judgment: Overflow while moving needs a browser at each width (rule 153 waits for Playwright); the proxy requires fresh shots.

rules.rule: No picture is drawn over text that is not its own.
rules.why_judgment: Overlap is visual; the proxy requires a fresh 390 shot.

rules.rule: On phones no small label is under 12px and each footer or menu link is at least a 24px tap target.
A nested list stays visibly nested.
rules.why_judgment: Nesting indent is rendered; the proxy requires fresh shots.

rules.rule: A separator (dot, slash, bar) never starts or ends a wrapped line.
rules.why_judgment: Line wrapping is rendered; the proxy requires fresh shots.

rules.rule: The URL scheme is frozen.
Keep every live URL, title, description, canonical, robots rule, H1 and heading outline, and every JSON-LD type, unless the owner approves the change.
A moved or merged page gets one 301 straight to its final address, never a chain.
Retired page groups answer 410 on purpose
A page that is gone answers 301 or 410, never a plain 404 for a URL people still ask for.
rules.why_judgment: Which 404s real crawlers ask for needs the logs after release; the proxy requires the release check entry.

rules.rule: No address on a retired host appears anywhere the site shows or gives Google.
Every state a reader can reach has its own URL:
Every indexable page names its own canonical, in the site's one address style
A title is 30 to 60 characters and 580px wide or less; a meta description is 120 to 155 characters and 990px or less, a full sentence, with no Markdown or HTML.
Each title and description is its own.
Every indexable page has a meta description, a title that fits, exactly one H1 and a share image.
Exactly one H1.
Keep old heading ids so old `#section` links still land
A page of a list after the first has its own title, description and H1
rules.why_judgment: List-page paging applies to the blog list only; the proxy checks title and canonical on each list page.

rules.rule: The sitemap lists only pages you want as search landing pages
Every indexable page is linked from the content of at least two other pages.
Every money page and hub has an internal-link plan built from its cluster and its data
A money page carries contextual links inside its prose
A post links up to its money page and across to two or three siblings, and they link back, with varied words
Link text names the page it goes to, and the same text never goes to two different pages.
A link to another site is `noopener`; add `nofollow` or `sponsored` on any link you do not vouch for or that is paid
No `` without an `href`, and no placeholder `href` such as `about:blank`. No `` without `src`
One spelling for the whole site
If a language or region is added later, every locale copy needs reciprocal hreflang, its own canonical, and the right `lang`
JSON-LD says what the page shows, and nothing else.
A FAQ has an answer for every question, never asks the same thing twice, and its FAQPage markup is the visible questions and answers, word for word, in the same order.
Structured data names only this site and the real people who write for it.
(Next.js adapter) Render JSON-LD (and any inline script a page emits first) inside an empty block `<div>`, never as the page's first child
With a sticky header, set `html { scroll-padding-top }` to the header height plus a gap
(Next.js adapter) The build stays fully static where the site is static: the build must succeed with every route generated at build time
Keep the speed scores where they are today.
rules.why_judgment: Lighthouse scores need a browser run; the proxy requires the run filed after the last commit and the static speed checks.

rules.rule: The build output is the same twice.
Analytics and ad tags run only on the real domain, not on previews or localhost, and heavy tags wait for the first interaction or a short delay.
Only one module reads the content files
Run only the checks the change touches; never the whole suite "to be safe".
rules.why_judgment: Which tests a change touches is decided per change; the proxy requires the change->check map in tools/checks.sh.

rules.rule: Look at the production build in a real browser at 360, 390, 820, 1280 and 1920 wide.
rules.why_judgment: A look in a real browser is human; the proxy requires fresh shots at all five widths and a page read from a production build.

rules.rule: Keep a regression test: from a scrolled page, navigate to several routes and click the logo, and assert `window.scrollY === 0`; also check one hash link
rules.warn_reason: The site has no Playwright yet; adding it needs the owner's yes (rule 107, open). WARN until then, FAIL after.

rules.rule: Check the page the way readers' tools show it:
rules.why_judgment: Reading the preview is human; the proxy requires the look filed after the last commit and the share tags.

rules.rule: The lead checks every page an agent produces
rules.why_judgment: Checking an agent's page is human; the proxy requires a dated review file that answers the kit's checklist, and fails a money figure in the head that the body never states.

rules.rule: Fix the bug, then add a guard for its whole class and sweep for siblings.
rules.why_judgment: Which guard covers a bug's class is judgment; the proxy requires the page's guard tests.

rules.rule: Before you tell the owner to look, make sure the page renders.
A check that makes a temp folder removes it, pass or fail.
Reviews happen on localhost previews from branch worktrees
rules.why_judgment: Where the owner reviews is a habit; the proxy requires a branch worktree.

rules.rule: Never push to the production branch and never merge without the owner's explicit yes in the current conversation
Production deploys only from a clean, up-to-date production branch
rules.why_judgment: A manual deploy leaves no trace in git; the proxy fails any main commit without a logged yes.

rules.rule: A yes covers what it names.
rules.why_judgment: What a yes covers is the owner's words; the proxy requires the decision filed in the journal.

rules.rule: Scheduled content publishes by its date, and the schedule really runs
rules.why_judgment: Publish timing is a release choice; the proxy fails unlogged main commits.

rules.rule: Commit with the repo's local identity
Never commit secrets, tokens or old export files
Before a redesign or a bulk change, make a backup tag, test the change on one real page first, and roll it out only on the owner's yes.
Components change markup, not wording, unless the owner approved the copy change.
rules.why_judgment: Whether wording changed is a diff a person reads; the proxy fails a changed title/H1 without a journal reason.

rules.rule: Do not re-run one-off migration scripts over live content.
Commit by path, with one plain sentence and the co-author line.
Files stay under 1,000 lines.
No commands that trigger permission prompts for nothing:
rules.why_judgment: Prompt-free commands are a habit; the proxy fails leftover scratch folders.

rules.rule: At most the project's agent limit at a time (default 4), none that starts its own agents, each closes its browsers, and a finished agent ends
rules.why_judgment: Live agents are not visible to a program; the proxy fails more than 4 open worktrees.

rules.rule: Know the undo before you merge:
rules.why_judgment: The undo and the live look happen at merge time; the proxy requires the release entry (stage release).

rules.rule: Keep this rulebook and `BRAND.md` current
Write to the owner in simple English, answer first, one question at a time.
rules.why_judgment: Plain English is judgment; the proxy fails long sentences in the steps log.

rules.rule: Find things yourself rather than asking, and when the owner points at a problem, fix the real page now.
rules.why_judgment: Fixing now vs queueing is behaviour; the proxy fails open findings older than 7 days.

rules.rule: Every URL and every text value someone may paste gets copy buttons, on the public site too
Every booking button opens the one shared booking dialog
Every call to action reports itself
Every dialog and bottom sheet opens over a dimmed backdrop, on a solid panel
After every FAQ comes one ask card
A call to action inside a post is the shared ask card
A post may carry `takeaways:` in its frontmatter: 3 to 5 one-line points
Every article has its reading aids
Every FAQ is one numbered box
The footer has a call row and Back to top
Motion is wanted on every page
A post's own Markdown gets its shapes by pattern
A ranked list post ("best ... software") opens with a lineup, and every tool named on a page shows its own logo
Every list of posts and every hub card shows the post's cover as a thumbnail, and every hub has its own interactive, animated element with its state in the URL
A post may mark a definition, a stat or a tip as a side note,
rules.why_judgment: Where a side note fits is editorial; the proxy fails a side-note number missing from the text.

rules.rule: Contact carries the About page's trust story, and About and Contact link every service page by name
A money page's first screen at 1280 to 1920 px is split: the words on the left, the page's own picture or tool on the right
Markdown copies of pages and `llms.txt` (waits for the owner)
A real author page and a compact author box on every post (waits for the owner)
rules.why_judgment: Waits for the owner and the author; the proxy fails any company-as-Person or url-less Person.

rules.rule: One Organization node for the whole site
Tests guard the FAQ markup
If AI answers or the top search results state a wrong fact on the page's topic (a price model, a limit), the page states the right one in its first screen, with its source
rules.why_judgment: Which AI facts are wrong needs reading the answers; the proxy requires 10+ US AI-answer runs in 30 days.

rules.rule: The words-only rules get their checks
The speed baseline is written down and kept
After each release, read the host's server errors (5xx) and the cron and API routes once
rules.why_judgment: Server errors appear after release; the proxy requires the release entry (stage release).

rules.rule: A new or rebuilt page keeps every house feature of its type
No two sibling pages share a hero, a fold design or an animation
rules.why_judgment: Sibling likeness is visual; the proxy fails a hero component shared with a sibling.

rules.rule: Before showing any page, look at every screen at 1366 and 390 px as a demanding designer
rules.why_judgment: A designer's eye is human; the proxy requires 1366 and 390 shots newer than the last commit.

rules.rule: The look of a page is measured in a real browser at 1440x900 and 390x844, and these limits fail the gate
Every product screenshot on a page has its capture date in the repo
Click every button, tab, slider and toggle on the page in a real browser before you show it
rules.why_judgment: Clicking needs a browser and eyes; the proxy requires a click-through filed after the last commit.

rules.rule: No rule is dropped because it is "not in our notes"
No shortcuts: copy every playbook step into the task; raise a skipped step before.
Work like a freelancer: run only the tests a change can affect.
rules.why_judgment: Per change; the proxy keeps the change->check map.

rules.rule: Workflows you can watch: multi-step jobs run as workflows.
One project at a time: no other project's names or facts.
Records match the work: a done step is ticked in place with its proof; no step left open behind done ones.
Log every instruction at once, before reporting.
Rules are code: every rule is registered with a check or a proxy; no loose words; the gate and hooks block.
No owner message goes unlogged: tools/owner_messages.py check passes before every report.
Engine vs project data: engine files hold no project facts (python3 tools/gate.py engine).
The owner reviews screens, not documents.
rules.row: The owner reviews screens, not documents
rules.why_judgment: How the owner is shown work is a habit; the proxy requires a live local URL and fresh shots.

rules.rule: Keep a page journal: every finding, question, decision and check.
Owner action items are their own list (journal/OWNER-ACTIONS.md).
rules.row: Owner action items are their own list

rules.rule: Primary market first: the US.
Simple English, answer first.
rules.why_judgment: Plain words are judgment; the proxy fails long sentences.

rules.rule: Decide page questions from evidence; claims, prices, offers and CTAs stay with the owner.
rules.why_judgment: Evidence quality is judgment; the proxy requires a journal reason for title changes and blocks never-claims.

rules.rule: At most 4 agents; model per job; each cleans up.
rules.why_judgment: Live agents are not visible to a program; the proxy counts worktrees.

rules.rule: Setup before page work: every doctor step OK.
Inventory first.
Money pages first, always.
rules.why_judgment: Choosing work is planning; the proxy requires the inventory marking money pages.

rules.rule: Snapshot every page we touch, before and after.
Measure every release at day 7, 14, 28, 56.
Money pages are unique: own dossier, hook, journey and interactive element.
Prototypes are real redesigns in the real site, on a branch, on a local URL.
rules.row: Prototypes are real redesigns, in the real site

rules.rule: Each cluster gets its own design.
rules.row: Each cluster gets its own design
rules.why_judgment: Design identity is visual; the proxy fails a shared hero.

rules.rule: Deep, not long: one fact in one place.
rules.why_judgment: Depth is judgment; the proxy fails repeated folds.

rules.rule: Hubs and lists show a cover on every card; every named tool shows its logo.
Claims: only what BRAND.md or the live site says.
rules.why_judgment: Matching a claim to the site needs reading; the proxy blocks the known bad claims.

rules.rule: Navigation lands at the top; every state has a URL; copy buttons.
rules.row: Navigation lands at the top; every state has a URL; copy buttons

rules.rule: The owner's yes before anything goes live.
rules.row: The owner's yes before anything goes live

rules.rule: Release one page at a time.
rules.row: Release one page at a time

rules.rule: The site stays as it is: Markdown in content/, no new CMS.
rules.row: The site stays as it is

rules.rule: Nothing starts with the computer.
Secrets only in ~/.config/<tool>/<site>.env.
Keep the remote private: it stays private until the owner says public.
rules.warn_reason: The gate cannot see a remote's visibility, so it warns and the owner confirms.
